chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Ali, who said:
I accompanied al-Rida (peace be upon him) during a journey and saw him praying the Maghrib prayer when the 'darkening' (fahmah) arrived from the east, meaning the blackness (of the sky).

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the tenth Imam, Ali ibn Musa)
key_terms.السَّوَادَ: The blackness (clarifying the meaning of fahmah)
key_terms.الْفَحْمَةُ: The darkening or blackness (referring to the sky after sunset)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific sign for the beginning of the Maghrib prayer time according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the precise onset of Maghrib time by identifying the 'fahmah'—the deepening darkness or blackness—as the visual marker, distinguishing it from the mere disappearance of the sun's disk. This aligns with the Shia juristic preference for the complete fading of the red twilight (shafaq) as the definitive end of the Maghrib window, ensuring the prayer is performed within its optimal time. The emphasis on direct observation underscores the practical application of celestial signs in establishing ritual timing.
